body:
## Type of Change
[x] ci - New workflow for CD
[x] feat - Added Dockerfile for containerization

**This workflow can't be run until it is merged in the main branch**

## Brief Description
Implemented the CD for this web application to be run in the production server in Digital Ocean(which has the public IP address `157.230.224.13`)
We can also trigger manually the deployment workflow
And added a Dockerfile specifically meant for production only

## Changes Made
- No modification to existing files was made
- Only added the Dockerfile and the workflow yml file to the repository

## How to test
The web app is actually running in the production server, but not from this workflow, but a workflow from a forked repository based from this repository, and can be seen running by going to this [link](http://157.230.224.13:3001/analytics), where the backend user app is also running
To test the Dockerfile and run the app in the container, we must first be in the `ucrconnect-dashboard` directory, and then build the image:
```bash
docker build -t frontend-app .
```

Then run the image in a container
```bash
docker run -d --name frontend-app -p 3001:3000 frontend-app
```

## Additional notes

Because the backend app also used the port 3000 and was deployed first, and both apps are running in the same server, this web app will be assigned to port 3001, but this does **not** mean that we should change the code the port this runs on and change it to the port 3001, because Docker is able to map ports from the host machine to the container running, so there is no need to change the code and make this app run in port 3001

  - Add `.venv/` to ignore virtual environment directory.

author: ryan180602
body:
## About The Pull Request

- Rebalances bows, crossbows. Adds a new type of arrow (steel bodkin) and rebalances the existing arrows. Pyroclastics no longer blow up, but they do set people on fire.
- Intended to make common iron arrows (now renamed to iron broadhead arrows) have low AP, low embed, higher damage (lower than current). While the less common steel arrows (steel bodkin arrows) have high AP (slightly higher than current), high embed (lower than current), low damage, higher accuracy
- Steel Bodkins travel slightly faster than Iron Barbed. Would likely need less leading.
- Smiths can craft Bodkins with 1 Steel ingot, to get 10x arrows. Bandits can buy it.
- Also adds limb accuracy to projectiles which rely on distance, skill, PER, type of weapon
- Changes up the damage calc formula and also gives crossbow lesser damage factor (now that recurve/longbows won't hopefully be as broken)
- Accuracy Factor dictates how much accuracy buffs you get for using a specific projectile weapon (alongwith your PER and bow/crossbow skill). Accuracy overall dictates chance to hit your targeted bodypart, and if missed, will hit the chest by default.
- Bow damage is dictated by damfactor of the weapon, and perception of the user (but now only if their PER is above 10).
- MAA Skirmishers lose their longbows, and get a recurve instead.
- Crafting longbows takes level 4 crafting, now.
- Shields lose omnidirectionality on arrow blocking. Passive coverage at maximum is 50%, overall lowered.

Proper numericals below.

## Testing Evidence

Using this space for numericals. Testing has been done, but it'd be best TM'd and tweaked.

All the calculations are done at **EXPERT** Bow/Crossbow with a PER of **12**. Upper range for values is at full charge.

1. `RECURVE BOW` (**1 DAMFACTOR, 1 ACCFACTOR**)
 _Iron Arrow (COMMON)_ - 40-48dam, 20AP, 15%-30%Embed, 65%baseAcc (will defeat upto light and regular leathers and blocked with most. Struggles against Otavan halfplates and light brigandines.)
_Steel Arrow (SMITH/BANDIT)_ - 25-30dam, 45AP, 40%-80%Embed, 75%baseAcc (will defeat most light armour and struggle against mediums. Struggles against regular gambeson)

2. `LONGBOW` (**1.2 DAMFACTOR, 0.9 ACCFACTOR**)
_Iron Arrow (COMMON)_ - 40-57.6dam, 20AP, 15%-30%Embed, 65%baseAcc
_Steel Arrow (SMITH/BANDIT)_ - 25-36dam, 45AP, 40%-80%Embed, 75%baseAcc

3. `CROSSBOW` (**1.2 DAMFACTOR, 1.1 ACCFACTOR**)
_Bolt_ - 84dam, 50AP, 100%Embed (Unchanged outside of the accuracy and damfactor)

## Why It's Good For The Game

Pyroclastics aren't fucking stupid anymore.

Shields now have at a maximum of 50% directional passive coverage (only with kite shields). Block intent is 100% but is monodirectional, now.
Damage is multiplied against simple/carbon NPCs. Different factors for different arrows.

The PR more-or-less works (pending test tweaks on live) even without the new bodkin arrow/iron arrow changes. If wanted, can remove bodkins altogether and normalise the standard iron arrow.

Thanks to Ansari and Rebel for ideas.

Will need some dev to put up the changelong before TM.

Ping @reen062 for shitfests

Code changes in #324 increased the recording time to 3 seconds.

 message to be tested on failure.

author: kraftp
body:
You can now specify a timeout for a workflow (in seconds, as a float):

```python
with SetWorkflowTimeout(my_timeout):
  my_workflow()
```

This also works with queues:

```python
with SetWorkflowTimeout(my_timeout):
  queue.enqueue(my_workflow)
```

And from clients:
```python
options: EnqueueOptions = {
    "queue_name": "my_queue",
    "workflow_name": "my_workflow",
    "workflow_timeout": 0.1,
}
client.enqueue(options, args)
```

When the timeout expires, the workflow is cancelled. This immediately sets its status to CANCELLED, removes it from any queues it is in, and preempts it at the start of its next step.

Semantics:

- Timeouts are **start** to completion. If a workflow is enqueued with a timeout, the timeout does not start until the workflow is dequeued.
- Deadlines **propagate**. When a workflow starts, a deadline is computed from its start time and the timeout. This deadline propagates to all the workflow's children, so when the deadline is reached, they are all cancelled. To override the deadline start a child with `SetWorkflowTimeout()`  You can use `SetWorkflowTimeout(None)` for no timeout.

author: nkaleth
body:
This pull request introduces user authentication to the application, ensuring that certain actions are restricted to authenticated users and improving error handling. Key changes include the addition of an authentication mechanism, updates to the `PostsController` to enforce user-specific access, and enhancements to the test suite to cover these new features.

### Authentication Mechanism:
* Added a `Secured` module with an `authenticate_user!` method to validate user tokens from the `Authorization` header. This method sets the `Current.user` context if the token is valid (`app/controllers/concerns/secured.rb`).
* Created a `Current` class to store the current user context using `ActiveSupport::CurrentAttributes` (`app/models/current.rb`).
* Implemented a `TokenGenerationService` for generating secure authentication tokens (`app/services/token_generation_service.rb`).
* Updated the `User` model to generate an authentication token after initialization (`app/models/user.rb`).

### Updates to `PostsController`:
* Included the `Secured` module and added `before_action :authenticate_user!` to restrict `create` and `update` actions to authenticated users (`app/controllers/posts_controller.rb`).
* Modified the `show`, `create`, and `update` methods to enforce user-specific access and ensure users can only interact with their own posts (`app/controllers/posts_controller.rb`).

### Test Suite Enhancements:
* Added a new test suite (`private_posts_spec.rb`) to verify authentication behavior for `GET`, `POST`, and `PUT` actions, including scenarios for valid and invalid tokens (`spec/requests/private_posts_spec.rb`).
* Removed outdated tests for unauthenticated post creation and updates from `posts_spec.rb` (`spec/requests/posts_spec.rb`).
* Updated the `users` factory to remove hardcoded `auth_token` values (`test/factories/users.rb`).This pull request introduces user authentication for creating and updating posts in the application. It includes changes to enforce authentication, generate and manage user tokens, and add test coverage for authenticated requests.

### Authentication Implementation:

* [`app/controllers/posts_controller.rb`](diffhunk://#diff-41547fca0ee5b1e4a7a2be25356b71d2fc7389aa1e86fe97fc10cd6f48d1c6dbR2-R3): Added a `before_action` to enforce user authentication for `create` and `update` actions. Introduced the `authenticate_user!` method to validate the `Authorization` header and set the `Current.user` context. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-41547fca0ee5b1e4a7a2be25356b71d2fc7389aa1e86fe97fc10cd6f48d1c6dbR2-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-41547fca0ee5b1e4a7a2be25356b71d2fc7389aa1e86fe97fc10cd6f48d1c6dbR50-R63)
* [`app/models/current.rb`](diffhunk://#diff-90f7d738b8d390337f1d6039b1e0c8ad2fe8d70de0a73e91f2b82cac11f65e5fR1-R3): Created a `Current` class using `ActiveSupport::CurrentAttributes` to store the current authenticated user.

### Token Management:

* [`app/models/user.rb`](diffhunk://#diff-9802ca3c9c4cf89904fd44bc114e35ebdf2c5dd3d5b645491e2b253e1afef29bR6-R13): Added an `after_initialize` callback to generate an authentication token for users using the `TokenGenerationService`.
* [`app/services/token_generation_service.rb`](diffhunk://#diff-3eb590850256ff7f24c8ef160b484afd84b246a49864209c6f770eb68b9e06bfR1-R5): Implemented a service class to generate secure random tokens for user authentication.

### Test Coverage:

* [`spec/requests/private_posts_spec.rb`](diffhunk://#diff-1c87a327ca68344f36a64e2d87d07db36fffe15ebf6777c9cc022f74d1a0482aR1-R52): Added request specs to test authenticated access to posts, including scenarios for authorized and unauthorized access to public and draft posts.

### Factory Updates:

* [`test/factories/users.rb`](diffhunk://#diff-c91e91c90ad64ef927f9ab367f21372a350dd5113158ef13c829ef075aa1d74bL5): Removed the hardcoded `auth_token` value to allow dynamic token generation during user creation.

author: sykwer
body:
## Description

Agnocast was previously reverted at https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/5986, but this pull request reintroduces it. The revert was originally done due to two issues:
- Although agnocast-heaphook and agnocast-kmod were distributed via the PPA server conforming to semantic versioning, the PPA server has a specification that automatically disables the previous version upon a new release.
- agnocast-kmod did not support certain Linux kernel versions (particularly 5.10).

These issues have now been resolved, so Agnocast is being reintroduced.

To address the limitation of the PPA, we separated the packages at the patch version level (`major.minor.patch`). For example, even if `v2.1.1` is released, the release of `v2.1.0` will no longer be discontinued, as they are now distinct packages (`agnocast-kmod-v2.1.0`, `agnocast-kmod-v2.1.1`, etc.).

## How was this PR tested?
```
./setup-dev-env.sh
sudo modprobe agnocast
sudo modprobe -r agnocast
dkms status
dpkg -L agnocast-kmod
dpkg -L agnocast-heaphook
```


## Notes for reviewers

None.

## Effects on system behavior

None.

body:
Since we can't easily put dynamic secret in environment variables for a service being run by systemd, we intead use their `LoadCredentials=` mechanism. For this to work the application needs to be designed to look in the location designated by the `CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY` variable. See https://systemd.io/CREDENTIALS/ for more details than you really want to know.

Change the GitHub token loading check at startup to probe this location for a file named `github` and if present, use that as the secret to access the GitHub API.

If the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable is set it will supersede the credentials mechanism.

body:
This pull request enhances the entity selector in the Slack snooze modal by only showing entities from signal instances associated with the given case.

#### Key Changes:

1. **Service Layer Enhancements:**
   - Updated the `get_all_desc_by_signal` function in `src/dispatch/entity/service.py` to accept an optional `case_id` parameter. This allows the function to filter entities not only by signal but also by case, if provided.

2. **Slack Plugin Modifications:**
   - Modified the `snooze_button_click` function in `src/dispatch/plugins/dispatch_slack/case/interactive.py` to pass the `case_id` when retrieving entities, ensuring that only relevant entities are displayed.
   - Updated the `create_action_buttons_message` function in `src/dispatch/plugins/dispatch_slack/case/messages.py` to use `case_button_metadata` for button actions, aligning with the new case-based filtering logic.
   - Enhanced the `entity_select` function in `src/dispatch/plugins/dispatch_slack/fields.py` to include the `case_id` parameter, filtering the dropdown to show entities from only signals in the case.

3. **Testing:**
   - Added new test cases in `tests/entity/test_entity_service.py` to verify the behavior of `get_all_desc_by_signal` with and without the `case_id` parameter. These tests ensure that the function correctly filters entities based on the provided case.

Release notes
Package name: socket.io
  • 4.8.1 - 2024-10-25

    Bug Fixes

    • bundle: do not mangle the "_placeholder" attribute (ca9e994)

    Dependencies

    • engine.io-client@~6.6.1 (no change)
    • ws@~8.17.1 (no change)
  • 4.8.0 - 2024-09-21

    Features

    Custom transport implementations

    The transports option now accepts an array of transport implementations:

    import { io } from "socket.io-client";
import { XHR, WebSocket } from "engine.io-client";

const socket = io({
  transports: [XHR, WebSocket]
});

    Here is the list of provided implementations:

    Transport Description
    Fetch HTTP long-polling based on the built-in fetch() method.
    NodeXHR HTTP long-polling based on the XMLHttpRequest object provided by the xmlhttprequest-ssl package.
    XHR HTTP long-polling based on the built-in XMLHttpRequest object.
    NodeWebSocket WebSocket transport based on the WebSocket object provided by the ws package.
    WebSocket WebSocket transport based on the built-in WebSocket object.
    WebTransport WebTransport transport based on the built-in WebTransport object.

    Usage:

    Transport browser Node.js Deno Bun
    Fetch ✅ ✅ (1) ✅ ✅
    NodeXHR ✅ ✅ ✅
    XHR ✅
    NodeWebSocket ✅ ✅ ✅
    WebSocket ✅ ✅ (2) ✅ ✅
    WebTransport ✅ ✅

    (1) since v18.0.0
    (2) since v21.0.0

    Added in f4d898e and b11763b.

    Test each low-level transports

    When setting the tryAllTransports option to true, if the first transport (usually, HTTP long-polling) fails, then the other transports will be tested too:

    import { io } from "socket.io-client";

const socket = io({

author: oo0oo0oooooo
body:
## Issue
This bug prevents damage from being applied consistently when using IceSpikeBlast and IceBlast. When a player is hit with IceSpikeBlast or IceBlast during the `bPlayer.slow(slowCooldown)`  the attack wouldnt pass through the `if(bPlayer.canBeSlowed())` check where the damage command for players is located.

## Additions
* Adds a SlowCooldown parameter to the config under "Abilities.Water.IceBlast.SlowCooldown".
* IceBlast uses new SlowCooldown parameter.
    
## Fixes
* Line 98 IceSpikeBlast
    > * Moves damage out of the `canBeSlowed()` check.
* Line 165 IceBlast
    > * Moves damage out of the `canBeSlowed()` check.

## Removals
* Line 99 IceSpikeBlast
    > * Removes recasting of entity to get the bending player. Now uses the same method as IceSpikePillar to get the bending player.

author: pedrozavalat
body:
This pull request introduces several changes to the `rcer_iot_client_pkg` library, focusing on improving import paths, error handling, and test configurations. It also includes updates to the versioning and changelog. Below is a summary of the most important changes, grouped by theme:

### Versioning and Metadata Updates:
* Updated the version in `pyproject.toml` to `0.1.2` and added a new entry in the `CHANGELOG.md` for version `0.1.1`, documenting a fix for absolute path issues.

### Import Path Simplifications:
* Replaced absolute import paths with relative imports across multiple files, such as `__init__.py`, `api.py`, and `test_update_thies_data_controller.py`, to improve maintainability and readability. 
### Error Handling Improvements:
* Introduced more specific exception handling in methods like `_async_start` in `aioftp_client.py` and `_initialize_sharepoint_client` in `update_thies_data.py`. For example, replaced generic `Exception` with `ConnectionError` or `RuntimeError` where applicable. 
* Updated HTTP status codes in `update_thies_data.py` to use `.value` for consistency and replaced some `500` status codes with `400` for better alignment with error semantics.

### Test Suite Enhancements:
* Refactored test imports to use relative paths and updated test case assertions to reflect the new error-handling logic, such as changing expected status codes from `500` to `400`. 
* Simplified the `conftest.py` setup to dynamically determine the parent directory for the Python path.

### Codebase Cleanup:
* Removed unused imports (e.g., `os`) and redundant comments to streamline the codebase. 
These changes collectively enhance the maintainability, error robustness, and testing reliability of the library.

author: damianvtran
body: # PR Description ## Summary of Changes This PR improves the user experience around model selection and working directory management in the UI. Key changes include: - Fix unpredictable scrolling by refactoring the scroll to bottom hook and general behaviour. Uses a fixed anchor in the scroll container in the messages view - Modified `HostingSelect` component to automatically refresh the model list when the hosting provider is changed. - Refactored and simplified the model refresh logic in `ModelSelect` to use a simple debounce, removing previous complex throttling and retry limits. - Added IPC handlers in the main process (`select-directory`, `get-home-directory`) for native directory selection and retrieving the user's home path. - Exposed `selectDirectory` and `getHomeDirectory` functions via the preload script (`window.api`). - Updated `DirectoryIndicator` component to utilize the new `getHomeDirectory` function and prepare for using `selectDirectory` (further changes likely needed). - Ensures the available model list is automatically updated when the user selects a different hosting provider. - Simplifies the logic for refreshing models, making it more reliable. - Adds backend support for using the native OS dialog to select a working directory. - Provides access to the user's home directory path for UI display purposes (e.g., shortening paths). ## Related Issue(s) Link any related issue or feature request (e.g., closes #123): - Related: #... _(Please link if applicable)_ ## Impact Describe the impact of these changes on the codebase: - Improves UX by ensuring model lists are up-to-date relative to the selected hosting provider. - Refactors model refresh logic for better maintainability. - Adds new IPC communication channels between the main and renderer processes for directory handling. - No breaking changes anticipated. - No direct dependency updates identified in this diff, but relies on Electron's `dialog` and `app.getPath` modules. ## Testing Details - How were these changes tested? Manual testing within the Electron app. - What specific scenarios were validated? - Changing the hosting provider in `HostingSelect` correctly triggers a model list refresh. - The `ModelSelect` component displays the updated list of models. - Verified console logs for model refresh triggers. - Tested the `selectDirectory` and `getHomeDirectory` IPC calls (e.g., via developer console or integrated component). - Checked that the `DirectoryIndicator` component correctly displays paths relative to the home directory (if implemented). - Mention any automated tests that were added or updated. - _(Add details if unit/integration tests were added/updated for hooks or components)_ ## Checklist - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project (ESLint/Prettier/Biome). - [x] I have performed a self-review of my code. - [x] I have added tests that prove my changes work as intended. - [x] All new and existing tests pass. - [x] I have run formatting, linting, and type checks, and they pass (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check`). - [x] I have updated the documentation when required. - [x] Security considerations are addressed (IPC communication is reviewed). - [x] I have linked all related issues. ## Screenshots (Optional)

author: haneepark
body:
Motivation:

- Preparing migration for the Documentation MDX content (almost done!)
- I thought it would be better to use plain CSS rather than Less for the following reasons:
  - Less, as well as Less variables, is no longer supported in Ant Design V5 ([V4 to V5 migration guide](https://ant.design/docs/react/migration-v5#technology-adjustment))
  - The old `antd-overrides.less` can't be used as is anyway, since global styles are defined using Infima instead of Ant Design. Infima variables are managed in `custom.css`
  - Less is not officially supported by Docusaurus (Plus, [docusaurus-plugin-less](https://www.npmjs.com/package/docusaurus-plugin-less) does not support Docusaurus v3)

Modifications:

- Add components:
  - RequiredDependencies (For usage , see `site-new/docs/required-dependencies-test.mdx`)
  - MaxWidth
  - TutorialSteps (For usage, see each step page of the REST tutorials in `site-new/docs/tutorials/rest/*`)
- Add a plugin that collects tutorial metadata from the front matter for TutorialSteps component
- Remove Less and use CSS instead
- Create a CSS file to customize Ant Design component style
- Add groupId for Tabs to sync tab choices
- Register some components to global components

author: ifergal
body:
## Description

This allows us to forward an OOBI to a new contact using the `/introduce` reply message. It will only work for KERIA agents that opt into it.

The `externalId` query param is also forwarded in our OOBI URL if it was in the contacts. This means the query param can contain a unique ID which could be shared embedded in an OOBI for a service via email. This allows the service to associate users (by email) with their wallet. This is just a temporary solution and a real solution should use proper KYC etc, since the email becomes a shared secret.

### Run extended test by pull request comment

Commands can be triggered by posting a comment with specific text on the pull request. It is possible to trigger multiple commands simultaneously.

```
extended-test --backstop | --integrated | --isolated | --record [--filter <file1>,<file2>,...,<fileN>]
```

#### Explanation

-   `--backstop` The command to run screen tests (optionally with keeping passing screenshots).
-   `--integrated` The command to run integrated tests against the live backend.
-   `--isolated` The command to run isolated tests against recordings.
-   `--record` The command to create new recordings for isolated tests.
-   `--filter` (Optional) A comma-separated list of test files to run. This parameter is valid only for the `--integrated`, `--isolated`, and `--record` commands.

#### Examples

```
extended-test --backstop
extended-test --backstop --keep-passing-screenshots
extended-test --integrated
extended-test --integrated --filter test1.spec.ts,test2.spec.ts
extended-test --isolated
extended-test --isolated --filter test1.spec.ts,test2.spec.ts
extended-test --record
extended-test --record --filter test1.spec.ts,test2.spec.ts
```

#### Commands for Bear platform working on branch rel/9.9

```
extended-test-legacy --backstop
extended-test-legacy --isolated
extended-test-legacy --record
```

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [jsonschema](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema) | dev-dependencies | minor | `0.29.0` -> `0.52.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Stranger6667/jsonschema (jsonschema)</summary>

### [`v0.52.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0520---2026-08-26)

##### Added

-   `Evaluation::is_valid`.
-   `Location::is_empty`.
-   `Display` for `ErrorEntry`.
-   `ValidationOptions::offline` and `canonical::CanonicalizeOptions::offline`, refusing to fetch references outside the registry.
-   `idna` Cargo feature, enabled by default, gating the `idn-hostname` and `idn-email` formats. [#​1313](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/issues/1313)
-   **CLI**: the `--offline` flag of `jsonschema validate`, `jsonschema bundle` and `jsonschema dereference`.

##### Changed

-   `ValidationErrors`' `Display` gained the instance path of each error.

##### Fixed

-   Canonicalization not idempotent where a `patternProperties` `$ref` matches a key `properties` names.
-   `is_valid` disagreeing with `validate`, `iter_errors`, and `evaluate` on a schema that reaches its own `$ref` twice, one of them under `not`.
-   `format: email` and `format: idn-email` rejecting an empty quoted string as the local part (it should be accepted).
-   `format: email` and `format: idn-email` rejecting an address literal whose `IPv6:` tag is not written in that exact case (the tag is case-insensitive).
-   `format: email` accepting a non-ASCII character in the local part (it should be rejected).
-   `ValidationOptions::with_draft` gating keywords on the vocabularies of the `$schema` it overrides, so the validator accepted every instance.

##### Performance

-   `iter_errors` collects into a single buffer instead of allocating and re-boxing an iterator at every schema node.

### [`v0.51.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0510---2026-08-23)

##### Added

-   `ValidationOptions::with_vocabulary` and the `vocabularies` attribute on `jsonschema::validator`, declaring support for a vocabulary this crate does not implement.
-   The `--vocabulary` flag of `jsonschema validate`.

##### Changed

-   `Vocabulary` gained the `FormatAssertion` variant, which its Draft 2020-12 URI parses to instead of `Vocabulary::Custom`, and is marked `non_exhaustive`.

##### Fixed

-   The `uniqueItems` length ceiling not reading an `items` or `contains` schema written as a `$ref`.
-   The Draft 2020-12 Format-Assertion vocabulary read as an annotation, so a meta-schema requiring it accepted values its `format` rejects.
-   An unrecognized `format` accepted under a meta-schema requiring the Format-Assertion vocabulary (it should be rejected).
-   A meta-schema requiring a vocabulary this crate does not implement accepted (it should be rejected).
-   The Draft 2019-09 Format vocabulary declared `true` read as an annotation, so a meta-schema requiring it accepted values its `format` rejects.
-   The bundled `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/meta/format-assertion` meta-schema not declaring its vocabulary, so a schema written against it annotated `format` instead of asserting it.
-   A meta-schema without `$id` keeping its `$vocabulary` unread, so a schema written against it got every Draft 2020-12 vocabulary.
-   A schema naming a bundled vocabulary meta-schema as its `$schema` rejected as an unknown meta-schema (it should build).
-   The `regex` format reading the Rust regex dialect (it should read the ECMA-262 dialect in Unicode mode).
-   The `uri-template` format rejecting an apostrophe in a literal (it should accept it, per RFC 6570 errata 6937).
-   The `duration` format accepting weeks combined with a time part, such as `P1WT1H` (it should reject it).
-   Stack overflow compiling `unevaluatedProperties` or `unevaluatedItems` beside a `$ref` that cycles back to the node, written as `#`, through its `$id`, or through a chain of definitions.

##### Performance

-   Building `unevaluatedProperties` or `unevaluatedItems` over a deep `allOf` or `$ref` chain costs its depth instead of its square.

### [`v0.50.1`](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0501---2026-08-22)

##### Changed

-   `CanonicalSchema::satisfiability` answers `Yes` for a string whose `pattern` or `format` a matching value can be built from.
-   `CanonicalSchema::satisfiability` answers `No` where a `format` takes no string of the length the schema asks for.

##### Fixed

-   `CanonicalSchema::negate` taking apart a union that reads a definition through its own `if`, so a schema and its negation shared a value.
-   `CanonicalSchema::subtract` dropping a Draft 4 array member an element demand partly takes.
-   `CanonicalSchema::covers` answering `Yes` where a Draft 4 element demand refuses a member.
-   A string schema whose `maxLength` is `0` keeping a `pattern`, `format`, or content facet unread, so the same constraints written in one object and written as an `allOf` reached different canonical forms.

##### Performance

-   `not` over a wide object schema costs its branch count instead of its square.
-   `not` over an object schema is linear in its property count, not quadratic.
-   `not` over an object schema with `additionalProperties: false` no longer costs cubic time in its property count.

### [`v0.50.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0500---2026-08-20)

##### Added

-   `CanonicalSchema::union` and `CanonicalSchema::subtract`.
-   `CanonicalizationError::UnsupportedResult`, reported where the canonical form does not support a set operation's result.
-   `OperandMismatch::DocumentRoots`, reported where both operands read `#` and it names a different document on each side.
-   **CLI**: `jsonschema validate -i INSTANCE` without a `SCHEMA` argument validates each instance against the schema named in its own `$schema` property. [#​1470](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/issues/1470)

##### Changed

-   `CanonicalSchema::is_satisfiable` is now `CanonicalSchema::satisfiability`, answering `Yes`, `No`, or `Unknown` - `Yes` wherever a value can be exhibited, not only for the forms listing their members.
-   `CanonicalSchema::covers` decides through the difference as well: `No` where the argument keeps values the receiver rejects, `Yes` where nothing is left over.
-   `CanonicalSchema::is_subset_of` is now `CanonicalSchema::covers`, answering `Yes`, `No`, or `Unknown` for whether the receiver admits every value the argument admits.
-   `CanonicalSchema::negate` returns `Result` rather than `Option`.
-   `CanonicalizationError::UnmodeledOperand` is now `CanonicalizationError::UnsupportedOperand`, and means only that an operand is a `Raw` pass-through.
-   A conjunction over a `$ref` folds through the body it names, so canonicalizing a document and combining its parts with the set operations reach one form; a document holding a reference cycle keeps the form it had.

##### Fixed

-   Combining nodes of two different documents repointing a `$ref` to `#` at the combined result instead of the document it was written in, including one named by a definition the result keeps.
-   Intersecting a `$ref` whose target is `true` or `false`, which panicked.
-   A key constraint left un-narrowed once a run is out of intersections, which panicked on the next read of it.
-   `CanonicalSchema::covers` answering `Unknown` for a schema against itself, where that schema is a `$ref`.
-   `CanonicalSchema::union` keeping a `$ref` beside the schema it names, where the other three operations read through it.
-   `CanonicalSchema::covers` and `CanonicalSchema::subtract` cancelling two nodes written the same way whose `#` names a different document.
-   Two results accepting the same values comparing unequal over the part of their documents neithe

author: khemarato
body:
This PR adds `id=''` attributes to the `<h3>`s of Ajahn @brahmali 's Vinaya Terms Appendix. This will allow people to link to specific terms in the index by appending `#term` to the end of the Term Appendix URL.

I used [slugify](https://github.com/un33k/python-slugify) on the Pali terms to generate the ids and then exported the resulting HTML using [BS4](https://www.crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/bs4/doc/) and a custom attribute regularizer.
This regularization meant that some attributes which were previously coded with `"`s have been switched to the standard (for this project) `'`s   Also, all attributes have been alphabetized, so `<i translate='no' lang='pli'>`s have been standardized to `<i lang='pli' translate='no'>`

cc @ihongda @thesunshade and @sujato

author: plby
body:
Okay, the LP bounds have been computed for all $N\le 10\\,000$.  There was one more value $N=9\\,633$ for which the LP bound is not tight.  I collected all $11$ of these in a file called `Data/loose_lp_bounds.txt` which made it into my latest commit in my previous pull request https://github.com/teorth/erdos-guy-selfridge/pull/24 which already got merged.  The format is very similar to what I wrote in my previous comment there: https://github.com/teorth/erdos-guy-selfridge/pull/24#issuecomment-2811388882
```
155 46 155.00000000 sorted
155 47 154.45454545 sorted
765 237 765.00909091 sorted
765 238 764.51818182 sorted
1528 482 1528.00000000 sorted
1528 483 1527.60000000 sorted
1618 511 1618.00000000 sorted
1618 512 1617.51111111 sorted
1619 511 1619.00000000 sorted
1619 512 1618.51111111 sorted
2574 822 2574.00000000 sorted
2574 823 2573.53448276 sorted
2935 939 2935.00000000 sorted
2935 940 2934.62184874 sorted
3265 1049 3265.00517241 sorted
3265 1050 3264.70517241 sorted
5122 1654 5122.00335570 sorted
5122 1655 5121.68120805 sorted
5680 1840 5680.00131926 sorted
5680 1842 5679.61345646 sorted
9633 3145 9633.00000000 sorted
9633 3146 9632.93968254 sorted
```

First of all, I've incremented $T$ on each line so that it's much more obvious to read now.  (That's already been committed, but only includes half of the lines above.)  Each line reports what the LP bound is for a specific $N$ and $T$, with no need to add $1$ in your head in any circumstance.  I think that is much more straightforward!  In this PR, I have also included the actual LP bound in each case.  For example, the second line reports that for $N=155, T=47$, the LP maximum is less than $N$ and thus that $(N,T)$ pair is infeasible even for real numbers.  Because the dual is sorted in all cases, this does not even assume the factors are all less than $N$.  Note that for $N=5680$, the LP bound is $2$ off from the integer lower bound as opposed to just $1$ in the other cases.

For all but $N=9\\,633$, I have successfully run the integer LP for the larger $O(n^2)$ size (primal) instance I describe here: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2025/03/26/decomposing-a-factorial-into-large-factors/comment-page-1/#comment-687732

I have not yet understood the optimization @teorth  proposes in the response at https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2025/03/26/decomposing-a-factorial-into-large-factors/comment-page-1/#comment-687734 but I will do that next.

There have been no greater solutions for the big integer programs.  That is, for all $N\le 10\\,000$ (except maybe $N=9\\,633$ because it hasn't finished running), the following process has succeeded:
1. Compute the LP relaxation upper bound.  The program assumes all factors are at most $N$, but we can check whether the dual is sorted.  It has been in all cases, so this is an honest upper bound which might simply not be tight.  (For example, this proves $t(5\\,680)\le 1\\,841$.)
2. Compute the integer program lower bound, assuming all factors are at most $N$.  Because this is an explicit construction, this is an honest lower bound.  (For example, this proves $t(5\\,680)\ge 1\\,839$.)
3. If these match, great: this means the upper and lower bounds are proven tight!  Otherwise, solve the (much bigger) integer program *not* assuming all factors are at most $N$.  The result of step 3 has always matched the lower bound from step 2.  (For example, this proves $t(5\\,680)=1\\,839$.)

I will report when the big integer program for $N=9\\,633$ finishes as well.

body: In SLPVectorizer, when computing spill costs for a tree, we call `BasicBlock::getFirstNonPHIOrDbgOrAlloca()` without checking if its return value is an end iterator. This can occur if the basic block is a `catchswitch` block. Dereferencing this iterator in an assertions build with sentinel-tracking causes a crash. This patch commits a test which demonstrates this issue.

author: timmybird
body:
# Fix parameter names in team endpoints

## Description
This PR fixes an issue with the parameter names in the team endpoints. The FOGIS API expects `matchlagid` as the parameter name for both `GetMatchdeltagareListaForMatchlag` and `GetMatchlagledareListaForMatchlag` endpoints, but our client was incorrectly using `lagid`.

## Changes
- Changed parameter name from `lagid` to `matchlagid` in `fetch_team_players_json` method
- Changed parameter name from `lagid` to `matchlagid` in `fetch_team_officials_json` method
- Updated documentation in `docs/api_endpoints.md` to reflect the correct parameter names
- Updated `docs/user_guides/team_management.md` to clarify the use of match-specific team IDs
- Updated version to 0.2.4 in `setup.py`
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md` with the new version and changes

## Related Issue
This PR addresses the issue where the client was failing with 500 errors when calling the team endpoints.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing
Created a minimal test script that directly tests the API endpoints with the correct parameter names, and it successfully fetched both players and officials data.

## Note
The unit tests are currently failing because they expect the old parameter name. A separate issue (#99) has been created to update the tests and mock server to use the correct parameter names.

<!-- ℹ お読みください / README
PRありがとうございます！ PRを作成する前に、コントリビューションガイドをご確認ください:
Thank you for your PR! Before creating a PR, please check the contribution guide:
https://github.com/misskey-dev/misskey/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## What
<!-- このPRで何をしたのか？ どう変わるのか？ -->
<!-- What did you do with this PR? How will it change things? -->
- 一行で表示されることが意図されている箇所はline-heightを1にし、フォントサイズとレンダリングされる高さを一致させる
  - 当該箇所が多いためデフォルトでこの設定と見做す
    - Webデザイン業界ではたまにある
- 複数行で表示されることが意図されている箇所は従来のline-heightを使用

今まで複数行のテキストをレンダリングしていた個所を洗い出し専用のクラス`_mt`を付与する作業が若干面倒(まあ抜けがあったとして大きな問題があるというわけではないけども)

※とはいえそこが一行表示なのか複数行表示なのか明示するように改修することは、このPRに関わらずいつかはやらなければならないこと

## Why
<!-- なぜそうするのか？ どういう意図なのか？ 何が困っているのか？ -->
<!-- Why do you do it? What are your intentions? What is the problem? -->
要素の高さに小数点が含まれると、要素が隣り合ったときに1px分の隙間がレンダリングされてしまうなどのグリッチを引き起こすので、それを防止

高さが小数だとレンダリングパフォーマンスに悪影響を及ぼす可能性もある(未検証)

また、フォントサイズ = 高さという前提があればデザインがしやすくなるほか、環境によってデザインが崩れることを防止できる

author: eugene-doobu
body:
This pull request refactors the initialization logic in the `LiveAssetManager` and `EventBanner` classes to improve asynchronous handling and ensure better code maintainability. The most significant changes include converting coroutine-based methods to use `UniTask`, renaming variables for consistency, and updating the `EventBanner` initialization process.

### Refactoring to `UniTask` for Asynchronous Operations:
* Converted `InitializeEvent` to an asynchronous method `InitializeEventAsync` using `UniTask`, replacing coroutine-based calls with `UniTask.WhenAll` for parallel asynchronous operations. (`LiveAssetManager.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f6e54e53a3bf13357244a21a674ac3f4511c1a7e3a50a7d27ed69408f6d4ac51L104-R103) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f6e54e53a3bf13357244a21a674ac3f4511c1a7e3a50a7d27ed69408f6d4ac51L120-R122)
* Updated the `Start` method in `EventBanner` to `InitializeAsync`, utilizing `UniTask` for asynchronous initialization of event data. (`EventBanner.cs`, [nekoyume/Assets/_Scripts/UI/Widget/EventBanner.csL32-R36](diffhunk://#diff-50574043bf0484ccf21a7b4a6bbeab617bacf4d9a1396ba54c5035c780828b11L32-R36))

### Code Consistency Improvements:
* Renamed the variable `isMainnet` to `isMainNet` for consistent naming convention across the codebase. (`LiveAssetManager.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f6e54e53a3bf13357244a21a674ac3f4511c1a7e3a50a7d27ed69408f6d4ac51L281-R282) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f6e54e53a3bf13357244a21a674ac3f4511c1a7e3a50a7d27ed69408f6d4ac51L306-R307)

### EventBanner Initialization Enhancements:
* Modified the `Show` method in `EventBanner` to call `InitializeAsync` with `.Forget()` if the `LiveAssetManager` is not yet initialized, ensuring proper asynchronous initialization. The `noctx` linter finds sending http request without context.Context.
Making a http call without context makes cancellation, timeout, or tracing impossible.

This PR adds context to the http post call.

author: uruzfr
body:
Cette mise à jour ajoute des commentaires explicatifs dans :

le code Arduino (sensor-arduino),

le client Linux (LinClient.c),

le client Windows (WinClient.c).

Les commentaires permettent de mieux comprendre :

l’usage des bibliothèques et des ports,

les options disponibles en ligne de commande,

le fonctionnement du chiffrement César,

la lecture série et l’envoi UDP.

✅ Objectifs
Faciliter la lecture et la maintenance du code,

Aider les nouveaux contributeurs à comprendre plus rapidement la logique,

Préparer le terrain pour une future documentation plus complète.

📁 Détail des fichiers modifiés
Arduino/sensor-arduino : +59 lignes commentées

Client/LinClient.c : +162 lignes commentées

Client/WinClient.c : +197 lignes commentées

🧪 Tests
Code testé sur Arduino Uno avec capteur DHT11 et écran LCD 2x16

Client Linux et Windows compilés et testés avec envoi vers serveur UDP local

body:
<!-- 

## 코드 리뷰 팁

- 코드와 관련된 질문이 있다면, PR 본문에 적기 보다는 해당 코드를 선택하고 코멘트를 남겨주세요.
  - [참고: Adding comments to a pull request](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-comments-to-a-pull-request)

-->

## 체크 리스트
- [X] 미션의 필수 요구사항을 모두 구현했나요?
- [X] Gradle `test`를 실행했을 때, 모든 테스트가 정상적으로 통과했나요?

- [X] [프롤로그](https://prolog.techcourse.co.kr)에 셀프 체크를 작성했나요?
[프롤로그 링크](https://prolog.techcourse.co.kr/studylogs/4179)
  <!-- 작성한 셀프 체크의 링크를 남겨주세요. -->

## 객체지향 생활체조 요구사항을 얼마나 잘 충족했다고 생각하시나요?
### 1~5점 중에서 선택해주세요.

- [ ] 1 (전혀 충족하지 못함)
- [ ] 2
- [X] 3 (보통)
- [ ] 4
- [ ] 5 (완벽하게 충족)

### 선택한 점수의 이유를 적어주세요.
<!-- 이유 작성 -->

## 웹 개발 경험 체크
🌱 레벨2 시작 이전에, 웹 애플리케이션 개발 경험이 있나요?
- [ ] 아니오. 전혀 경험이 없습니다.
- [ ] 예. 예제 코드를 따라하거나 클론 코딩을 해봤습니다. (ex. 강의를 보고 따라함)
- [X] 예. 웹 애플리케이션을 만들었지만 로컬에서만 실행해봤습니다.
- [ ] 예. 웹 애플리케이션을 만들고 배포해봤습니다. (ex. 클라우드 혹은 리모트 서버에 배포)

## 어떤 부분에 집중하여 리뷰해야 할까요?
<!-- 리뷰어가 효과적으로 피드백할 수 있도록 중점적으로 리뷰 받고 싶은 내용을 *요약* 형태로 작성해 주세요.
리뷰해야 할 포인트를 요약해 강조해 주시면, 리뷰어가 코드 전체를 이 부분에 집중해 리뷰할 수 있습니다.
반면 특정 코드부분에 대한 피드백이 필요하다면, 이 곳에 적기 보다 해당 코드를 선택하고 코멘트를 남기는 것을 권장합니다. -->

안녕하세요 범블비! 😃

이번 미션에서는 페어 크루와의 이해를 맞춰가는 과정을 특히 중요하게 생각하며, 주어진 요구사항을 최대한 분석하고 함께 고민하며 개발을 진행했습니다.

기존에도 스프링을 사용해본 경험은 있었지만, 이번 과정을 통해 제가 스프링을 충분히 이해하지 못한 채 사용해왔던 부분들이 많았구나 하고 느꼈습니다.
리뷰를 통해 제가 사용하는 기술들에 대해 정확히 이해하고 있는지 점검받고 싶어요.

부족한 부분이 있다면 아낌없는 피드백 부탁드립니다! 감사합니다 🙏

---

### DTO 도입 여부

현재 Reservation 도메인 객체는 불변(immutable) 객체로 설계되어 있고,
상태 변경 없이 id, name, date, time 정도만 다루기 때문에
초기에는 도메인 객체를 그대로 요청/응답에 사용하는 방식으로 구현했습니다.

```java
public class Reservation {
    private final Long id;
    private final String name;
    private final LocalDate date;
    private final LocalTime time;
}
```

당시에는 다음과 같은 이유로 DTO를 도입하지 않았습니다.

 - Reservation은 불변 객체로 외부 노출 시 상태 변경 위험이 없고

 - 민감한 정보나 도메인 보호가 필요한 상황도 아니었으며

 - 클라이언트와의 요청/응답 포맷도 도메인 구조와 거의 동일했기 때문에

DTO의 주요 목적(도메인 보호, 응답 포맷 제어, 계층 분리 등)에 비춰봤을 때,
**DTO를 도입하지 않는 것이 더 단순하고 효율적인 구조**라고 판단했습니다.

그러나 이후 예약 목록을 관리하는 Reservations 클래스에서 **id를 별도로 관리**하게 되었고,
응답에 id 값을 포함해야 할 필요가 생기면서 결국 ReservationResponse DTO를 도입하게 되었습니다.

제가 DTO를 선택하게 된 판단이 현재 상황에서 타당한 결정이었는지,
아니면 여전히 도메인 객체를 그대로 사용하는 기존 방식도 적절한 선택이었다고 볼 수 있는지 궁금합니다.

---

### 📌 코드리뷰 질문 그라운드룰 (지우지 마세요)
✅ 많은 사람과 공유하고 토론해보는 것이 더 좋은 질문에는, 리뷰어가 💬말풍선 이모지를 남겨 토론을 추천할 수 있어요.  
✅ 토론을 추천받은 질문은 `#be-7기-잡담-질답`슬랙채널이나 캠퍼스에서 자유롭게 토론을 이어가보세요!  
✅ 코드에 대한 맥락 없이 리뷰어의 주관적인 의견을 묻거나, 단순히 현업에서는 어떻게 하는지를 묻는 질문은 코드 리뷰 본문에는 어울리지 않아요.  
코드 리뷰는 변경된 코드의 목적, 의도, 품질을 중심으로 논의하는 자리예요.  
✅ 코드와 관련된 질문이 있다면 PR 본문에 적기보다는, 해당 코드를 선택해 코멘트를 남겨주세요.

Clean up autotuner tests to prepare enabling dynamic search space

Makes all autotuner tests work with `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_dynamic_dot_search_space=1`:

- we create an `se::DeviceDescrpiton` with reasonable default values, since the new search space uses a lot of this information
- with larger split_k, we might end up creating a kInput, instead of a kLoop fusion, so we match either one in the tests
- all configs from b/337839570 seem to not be crashing anymore, so we no longer need to prevent generating them (I also added tests to verify that they in fact do not crash anymore)
- we removed sparsity support, so we don't need to support it in the autotuner
- Triton can't do anything useful with clusters, so we don't need to autotune them either

I didn't waste time making adjustments in the current implementation of the autotuner (e.g., allowing a wider set of configs, and removing sparsity support), since all of that code will anyway go away as soon as we land the dynamic search space.

author: penguineer
body:
This pull request introduces changes to improve MQTT client behavior by adding a custom disconnect handler and ensuring proper cleanup during application shutdown. The most important changes include adding a callback mechanism for handling unexpected MQTT disconnections, modifying the MQTT client creation process to support this callback, and ensuring the MQTT client disconnects cleanly before the application exits.

### MQTT disconnect handling:

* [`app.py`](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R30-R33): Added a new function, `mqtt_disconnect_handler`, to log a warning when the MQTT client disconnects unexpectedly while the application is running.
* [`mqtt.py`](diffhunk://#diff-26aadb984a310fe79440f307b9aeccb0c550911ae971bfad69f5f4721e0234feL53-R63): Updated the `on_disconnect` function to invoke a user-provided callback (`on_disconnect_cb`) if it is set in the `userdata`.

### MQTT client creation:

* [`mqtt.py`](diffhunk://#diff-26aadb984a310fe79440f307b9aeccb0c550911ae971bfad69f5f4721e0234feL53-R63): Modified the `create_client` function to accept an optional `on_disconnect_cb` parameter and pass it to the MQTT client via `userdata`.

### Application shutdown:

* [`app.py`](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R114): Updated the `main` function to explicitly disconnect the MQTT client before stopping its loop during application shutdown.

author: elijerald
body:
# Summary
This PR will resolve Issue #67  :"WebCampus API script", introducing a new python script to the repository (extract_data_canvas_api.py).

# Description
This PR introduces a Python script that interfaces with the Canvas LMS API to retrieve and process a variety of course-related data. The script provides a class-based structure (Canvas_api) to encapsulate logic for accessing course information, user details (students and professors), assignments, and associated file data. The main goal of this script is to extract and organize course content in a structured JSON format for further processing or analysis.

The Canvas_api class manages API authentication using an environment variable (WC_API_KEY) and provides dedicated methods to retrieve and print user data (students, professors, and all users), assignments, and course metadata (such as course name, code, and term ID). Additionally, the script includes logic to extract file links embedded within assignment descriptions using HTML parsing via BeautifulSoup.

The main() function serves as a demonstration of the class in action, with example method calls to test the functionality. Currently, the assignment data is used to extract embedded file links, though additional processing and data export steps can easily be integrated later.

While the script is functional, it is still in early stages. There is room for enhancements such as:

Improved error handling for API responses

JSON export of retrieved data

Modularization for broader use across multiple Canvas courses

Unit tests to ensure reliability and prevent regressions

# Documentation
None

# Unit Tests
The unit tests will be a new PR.

## About the PR <!-- Describe the Pull Request here. What does it change? What other things could this impact? -->
As it's configured right now, airlocks that look the same will share wire distributions. For example: any non-perspective external airlock shares wires regardless of access requirements, but they don't share with perspective external airlocks. I remember there being a good deal of disagreement about how to group doors, which is why that is isolated to its own proc. I've got an opinion, but mostly I wanted to get moving on the functionality already.

## Why's this needed? <!-- Describe why you think this should be added to the game. -->
Makes it potentially more difficult for folks to hack into places, since the bridge doors may not necessarily be hacked the same way as some random door in Butte-Aess, Maintenance that nobody will notice you testing on.

body:
This pull request enhances the documentation and notebooks by integrating links to pre-trained models and datasets hosted on Hugging Face, along with instructions for downloading them. It also introduces new sections for place recognition and point cloud registration in the documentation.

### Documentation Updates

* Updated `README.md` to include direct links to Hugging Face-hosted pre-trained model weights for place recognition and point cloud registration. Added instructions for accessing PaddleOCR weights and provided example code for downloading them.
* Enhanced `docs/source/index.rst` by replacing placeholder text with detailed sections for "Place Recognition," "Registration," and "PaddleOCR weights," including model descriptions, training datasets, and direct links to configuration files and weights.

### Notebook Enhancements

* Added instructions in `notebooks/test_cross_season/01_PlaceRecognitionPipeline.ipynb` for downloading datasets and model weights using `wget` commands. Included both place recognition and registration weights.
* Updated `notebooks/test_cross_season/02_SequencePointcloudRegistrationPipeline.ipynb` with similar instructions for downloading datasets and weights, tailored to the sequence point cloud registration pipeline.
* Introduced weight download instructions in `notebooks/test_cross_season/03_PlaceRecognitionPipeline_with_semantics.ipynb` for models with semantic inputs.
* Enhanced `notebooks/test_cross_season/04_ArucoLocalizationPipeline.ipynb` with dataset and weight download instructions for the ArUco-based localization pipeline.

author: sanyamaximyuk
peccneck
body:
## About the PR
Alters Resomi race's cold-based movement speed changes to match with their lower temperature tolerances (and parity with the UI element).

## Why / Balance
For an ice-world race, they sure do seem quite crippled in mobility by the slightest of breezes.

## Technical details
YML changes. Thresholds calculated based on the alert scale from TemperatureSystem and rounded up, where:
`ceil(((normalBodyTemperature - coldDamageThreshold) * alertThreshold) + coldDamageThreshold)`
with the alert thresholds being 0.66, 0.4, and 0.

This is also the same fashion in which they were calculated for BaseMobSpeciesOrganic (albeit it was rounded down there), so parity there as well.

# Backport

This will backport the following commits from `main` to `8.19`:
 - [[Security Solution][Rules Management] Separate actions import logic from rules import (#216380)](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/216380)

<!--- Backport version: 9.6.6 -->

### Questions ?

<!--BACKPORT [{"author":{"name":"Marshall Main","email":"55718608+marshallmain@users.noreply.github.com"},"sourceCommit":{"committedDate":"2025-04-16T15:47:26Z","message":"[Security Solution][Rules Management] Separate actions import logic from rules import (#216380)

## Summary

Redo of https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/193471
Closes https://github.com/elastic/security-team/issues/8644

> Fixes a bug where importing a rule fails with a connector into a space
where (1) the connector already exists, and (2) the existing connector
was exported and re-imported from another space. The import logic in
this scenario effectively tries to convert the action ID on the rule
import twice. The second conversion attempt tries to use the old action
ID to look up the correct new action ID in a map, however, in this test
scenario the action ID has already been updated by legacy SO ID
migration logic and there is no map entry with the new ID as a key. The
result is that the second attempt sets the action ID to undefined,
resulting in an import failure.

The root cause of the bug is that we have two different places in the
rule import logic where action IDs are migrated. The first ID migration
was done by `migrateLegacyActionsIds` prior to importing rule actions,
and the second migration was done by `importRuleActionConnectors` after
importing the actions. `importRuleActionConnectors` used a lookup table
to convert old IDs to new IDs, but if the connector already existed and
had an `originId` then the rule action would already be migrated by
`migrateLegacyActionsIds`. The lookup table used by
`importRuleActionConnectors` does not have entries for migrated IDs,
only the original IDs, so in that case the result of the lookup is
`undefined` which we assign to the action ID.

This PR reworks the logic to create a clean separation between action
and rule import. We now import the connectors first, ignoring the rules,
then migrate action IDs on the rules afterwards. This handles connectors
changing IDs in any way, either through the 7.x->8.0 migration long ago
or IDs changing on import if there are ID conflicts. Only after the
connectors are imported and rule actions are migrated do we then verify
if each rule action references a connector ID that actually exists with
the new `checkRuleActions` function, replacing
`checkIfActionsHaveMissingConnectors` and related functions that were
also buggy.

Finally, as a nice side effect this rework removes "rule action
connector missing" errors out of the `action_connector_errors` part of
the response. `action_connector_errors` is reserved for errors importing
connectors specifically. If a rule action is missing a connector and
therefore we don't import the rule, that's a rule error and it's
represented in the `errors` part of the response. Since the shape of the
response is not changing, I don't consider this a breaking change but
rather a bug fix.

## Repro Steps

Repro Steps
1. Download the export file below and change the extension back to
.ndjson from .json (github does not allow .ndjson files

[rules_export.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17065272/rules_export.json)
2. Import the rule and connector into a space (default is fine)
3. Create a new space
4. Import the rule and connector into the new space
5. Import the rule and connector into the new space again, but check the
`Overwrite existing connectors with conflicting action "id"` box.
Observe the failure.

---------

author: mildronize
body:
This PR enhances secret injection flexibility by allowing `targetPath` customization inside secret injection strategies.  
It also finalizes the cleanup of deprecated secret providers, aligning fully with Kubernetes conventions.

### 📦 What's Changed

- Add `targetPath` support to all secret injection strategies
- Remove deprecated classes:
  - `EnvSecretProvider` (replaced with `OpaqueSecretProvider`)
  - `ImagePullSecretProvider` (replaced with `DockerConfigSecretProvider`)
- Update examples and unit tests to match the new structure

### ✨ Why

- Allow fine-grained secret injection to arbitrary paths in Kubernetes resources
- Simplify complex multi-container or multi-resource secret injection scenarios
- Complete secret provider standardization and support custom path injection workflows

### 📌 Important Reminder

**Resource targeting validation already exists and behaves as follows:**

- When injecting using a standard kind like `'env'`, Kubricate will search for **exactly one** matching resource (e.g., a `Deployment`) in your stack.
  - If **no matching resource** is found → ❗ Throw error
  - If **multiple matching resources** are found → ❗ Throw error
  - If **exactly one** matching resource is found → ✅ Injection succeeds without requiring `.intoResource()`
- If you want to inject into a **different resource kind** (e.g., CronJob) or have multiple similar resources, you **must specify** `.intoResource(...)`.
- If you are using a **custom `targetPath`**, `.intoResource()` is **always required**.

#### Example 1: Simple `env` injection (no `.intoResource()` needed if exactly one match)

```ts
injector.secrets('MY_SECRET')
  .inject('env', { containerIndex: 0 }); // ✅ Works if exactly one Deployment is found
```

#### Example 2: Multiple Deployments or no match (must specify `.intoResource()`)

```ts
injector.secrets('MY_SECRET')
  .inject('env', { containerIndex: 0 })
  .intoResource('deployment_0'); // ✅ Required if multiple Deployments exist
```

#### Example 3: Inject using `targetPath` (must specify `.intoResource()`)

```ts
injector.secrets('my_app_key')
  .forName('ENV_APP_KEY')
  .inject('env', {
    targetPath: 'spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env'
  })
  .intoResource('cronJob'); // ✅ Required because of custom path
```

### 🔧 Migration Plan

| Before                        | After                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Use `EnvSecretProvider`       | Replace with `OpaqueSecretProvider`       |
| Use `ImagePullSecretProvider` | Replace with `DockerConfigSecretProvider` |
| No `targetPath` customization | Now supported                             |

No changes are required for stacks using default injection into Deployments without custom paths.

### 📈 Summary

This update improves secret injection flexibility, enables safe multi-resource injection workflows, enforces clear targeting rules, and fully completes the provider naming refactor.

author: staskus
body:
## Description Add missing analytics events for the POS Coupons implementation. Specs: Name | Event -- | -- Coupon settings enabled. Existing event with _pos prefix when the coupon is enabled. | `pos_coupon_settings_enabled` Coupon created. Existing event with _pos prefix when the coupon is created. | `pos_coupon_creation_success` Checkout with coupons Existing pos_checkout_tapped event with a new coupons_in_cart parameter. | `pos_checkout_tapped` New parameter:coupons_in_cart : Integer Checkout with coupons failed. Existing `pos_order_creation_failed` with improved error_context. | `pos_order_creation_failed` Update parameter:error_context to specific error `woocommerce_rest_invalid_coupon` rather than the whole error message since it's difficult to filter it out.

New Events

We will track the new data using the same conventions as products in POS.

Name | Event -- | -- Products section tapped. | `pos_products_tapped` Coupons section tapped. | `pos_coupons_tapped` Coupon creation tapped. |`pos_coupons_create_tapped` Coupons pull to refresh. | `pos_coupons_pull_to_refresh` Coupon added to the cart. | `pos_coupon_added_to_cart` Coupon removed from cart. Track also when "Remove coupon" button is tapped on an error. | `pos_coupon_removed_from_cart` ## Steps to reproduce Prerequisites: - Disable `Enable the use of coupon codes` setting in WooCommerce->Settings - Enable `enableCouponsInPointOfSale` feature flag 1. Open POS and switch to the Coupons tab -> `pos_coupons_tapped` should be tracked 2. Tap 'Enable Coupons' -> `pos_coupon_settings_enabled` should be tracked 3. Tap '+' -> `pos_coupons_create_tapped` should be tracked 4. Create a coupon -> `pos_coupon_creation_success` should be tracked 6. Add coupon to cart -> `pos_coupon_added_to_cart` should be tracked 7. Remove coupon from cart -> `pos_coupon_removed_from_cart` should be tracked 8. Pull to refresh -> `pos_coupons_pull_to_refresh` should be tracked 9. Add coupon and products to cart, tap checkout -> `pos_checkout_tapped` should be tracked with `coupons_in_cart` parameter and number of coupons added to cart 10. Return to edit order, add invalid coupon, checkout -> `pos_order_creation_failed` should be tracked with `error_context` set to `woocommerce_rest_invalid_coupon` Registration PRs of new events: - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2803 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2804 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2805 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2806 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2807 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2808 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2809 - https://github.com/Automattic/tracks-events-registration/pull/2810 ## Testing information Tested on iPad Air 11 Inch M2 iOS 18.2 Simulator --- - [x] I have considered if this change warrants user-facing release notes and have added them to `RELEASE-NOTES.txt` if necessary. ## Reviewer (or Author, in the case of optional code reviews): Please make sure these conditions are met before approving the PR, or request changes if the PR needs improvement: - [ ] The PR is small and has a clear, single focus, or a valid explanation is provided in the description. If needed, please request to split it into smaller PRs. - [ ] Ensure Adequate Unit Test Coverage: The changes are reasonably covered by unit tests or an explanation is provided in the PR description. - [ ] Manual Testing: The author listed all the tests they ran, including smoke tests when needed (e.g., for refactorings). Each PSL PR needs to have a description, rationale, indication of DNS validation and syntax checking, as well as a number of acknowledgements from the submitter. For an example of what an excellent description in a PR looks like

To be clear, it is appropriate to address how those limits impact 
your domain(s) directly with that third-party, and it is inappropriate

restrictions.
-->

<!--
The purpose of the question above is to expose limit workarounds.
If there are third party limits that the PR seeks to overcome, those
must be listed within the rationale section of this request, and 
provide a good level of detail the effort that was made to work directly 
with the third part(y|ies) in attempting to address this within their 
rationale response below.
In all cases, software and services should be discouraged from use of
the PSL as a rate-limiting tool, and provide clear instructions to their
own clients, partners and users on the manner in which they can directly
request rate limit increases.
We treat the following as an attestation in the public record of the 
requesting party that they are not attempting to bypass rate limits through
the PR.
-->

Submitter will maintain domains in good standing or may lose section.

The guidelines describe which section to place the entry, what the 
order of commented org placement, order of sorting of entries. 
(hint: TLD then SLD, ascending sorting) Although it seems pedantic, 
the sorting and formatting rules help ensure all of the automation

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a blockchain-based system for restaurant equipment maintenance using Clarity smart contracts for the Stacks blockchain. The system provides a comprehensive solution for tracking equipment, scheduling maintenance, verifying technicians, and ensuring regulatory compliance.

## Features

### Equipment Registration Contract
- Registration of restaurant kitchen equipment with detailed information
- Ownership tracking and transfer capabilities
- Equipment management functions (update, query)

### Service Scheduling Contract
- Maintenance schedule creation and management
- Service record tracking
- Due maintenance querying

### Technician Verification Contract
- Technician registration with credentials and specialties
- Equipment-specific certification tracking
- Verification system for qualified repair providers

### Compliance Tracking Contract
- Regulatory requirement definition and tracking
- Inspection recording
- Compliance status monitoring

## Implementation Details

- All contracts are written in Clarity (.clar) language
- Full test coverage using Vitest
- Clear documentation in README.md
- No external package dependencies as requested

## Testing

Tests have been implemented for all four contracts, covering the core functionality:
- Equipment registration and management
- Maintenance scheduling and recording
- Technician verification
- Compliance tracking

All tests pass successfully and provide good coverage of the contracts' functionality.

## Integration Points

The contracts work together through shared identifiers:
- Equipment IDs link equipment registration to service records and compliance
- Technician principals connect verification to service records
- Equipment types connect technician certifications to specific equipment

## Future Enhancements

Potential future improvements:
- Integration with IoT devices for automatic maintenance alerts
- Mobile app for technicians to access and update records
- Analytics dashboard for restaurant owners
- Integration with payment systems for service billing

## Requested Review Focus

Please focus review on:
1. Contract security and potential vulnerabilities
2. Data structure efficiency
3. Error handling
4. Function naming clarity
5. Test coverage completeness

### Summary
This Pull Request fixes functionality that handles requests to the Public API with wildcard versions (e.g., 2.*) that was previously returning unpublished data set versions.

It tweaks logic of Public API endpoints that accept data set version that user specifies, that if the user a wildcard dataset version, that only published dataset versions are returned. 

### Main Changes
Ensure that for wildcard data set version - only published data set versions are returned if present. 
Ensures 404 response if a non-published version exists and has been requested using wildcard parameter.

### Updates to tests:
Added or updated test coverage for controllers handling wildcard dataset version queries.
Extended existing tests to check the behavior for both published and non-published versions.
Introduced a new method WherePublishedStatus in dataset version query extension to filter only published versions.

## Proposed change

Since Systemd v256 the Range header must not end with a trailing colon. We relied on this undocumented feature when following logs, and the frontend or CLI may still use it in requests. To fix the requests failing with new Systemd version, intercept the header and fill in the num_entries to maximum possible value, which avoids the journal-gatewayd returning the response prematurely and also works on older Systemd versions.

The journal-gatewayd would still return response if follow flag is used along with num_entries, but this behavior is unchanged and would be better fixed in the backend.

author: ibrahim-haizel
body:
# PR: Implement Search Component

This pull request introduces a new `Search` component with an accessible and customisable design, along with detailed usage examples and code snippets. The changes include adding the `IconSearch` component, creating a comprehensive examples page, and providing reusable code blocks for the `Search` component's various configurations.

Built to match the [GOV.UK Publishing Components Search component guide](https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/search).

### New `Search` Component and Icon:

* Added a new `IconSearch` component (`src/lib/icons/IconSearch.svelte`) that renders a scalable SVG search icon with customisable styles.

#### Key Features Implemented

- **Core GOV.UK Functionality:** Renders a standard search box with an associated label and submit button, suitable for use within a `<form>`.
- **Label Flexibility:** Supports standard labels, inline labels (absolutely positioned over the input), labels wrapped in heading tags, and labels with custom sizing (`label_size`).
- **Styling Variants:** Includes styles for standard white backgrounds (`on_govuk_blue: false`), dark blue backgrounds (`on_govuk_blue: true`), a specific `homepage` variant (which requires `on_govuk_blue`), and a `large` size variant.
- **Width Control (`input_width`):** Allows setting the maximum width of the entire component using GOV.UK width utility classes (e.g., `govuk-!-width-two-thirds`).
- **Hint Text (`hint`):** Supports optional hint text displayed below the label and linked via `aria-describedby`.
- **Customisation:**
  - `label_custom_class`: Allows adding custom CSS classes to the label.
  - `button_background_color`: Allows setting a custom background color for the submit button.
  - Standard props for IDs, names, ARIA attributes, data attributes, etc.
- **Accessibility:** Includes appropriate ARIA attributes and visually hidden text for the button.

#### Technical Highlights

- **`label_custom_class` Handling:** To prevent CSS conflicts, the component intentionally _does not_ apply its default styling classes (`gem-c-search__label` or `govuk-label`) when `label_custom_class` is provided. This gives the custom class full control but may require users to also set `inline_label={false}` and potentially add spacing utilities for desired layout.
- **Conditional Styling:** The `button_background_color` is applied via an inline style, which is explicitly overridden by the component's CSS classes when the `on_govuk_blue` or `homepage` variants are active.
- **Class Management:** Uses `clsx` for efficient and readable conditional class application.
- **Automatic ID Generation:** Generates a unique ID for the input/label association if `label_id` is not provided (client-side only).

### Examples and Documentation:

* Created an examples page (`src/wrappers/components/ui/search/Examples.svelte`) showcasing 18 use cases of the `Search` component, such as setting custom labels, sizes, accessibility attributes, and styles.

### Reusable Code Snippets:

* Added a `codeBlocks.js` file (`src/wrappers/components/ui/search/codeBlocks.js`) containing reusable code snippets for each example, making it easier to integrate and replicate specific configurations.

### Further Work

Testing required as well as build upon this component to create auto suggestions version.

This PR makes the node score a combination of number of applications and number of unfulfilled interfaces.

author: gabrielmfern
body:
Addresses #2051. The previous behavior was to always give priority to the `margin` shorthand property, and now it gives priority according to how the properties come in, exactly how React does it itself. 

So, if the user comes in with something like

```jsx
<Text style={{ margin: 0, marginBottom: '1rem' }}/>
```

it will compute the margins as `{ marginTop: 0, marginRight: 0, marginLeft: 0, marginBottom: '1rem' }`

This fix that maintains the order of styles provided by the user is also going to need to be done in the Button since it currently does a set priority similar to what the Text component did before this PR.

body:
### 📣 Summary
Fixed server errors caused by unexpected permission mutations in views using `DjangoModelPermissions`.

### 📖 Description
This PR resolves 500 Internal Server Errors occurring when accessing certain endpoints of the v1 API. The issue was caused by an unintended mutation of the `perms_map` attribute in classes inheriting from DjangoModelPermissions.

Since perms_map is shared across instances, modifying it dynamically introduced side effects across views and requests. This fix prevents the mutation and ensures that permission handling remains isolated and reliable across the API.


### 👀 Preview steps

Bug template:
1. ℹ️ have an account and a project
2. preview the project

author: dasionov
body:
This change enables the `node-labeller` routine for ARM64-based clusters in KubeVirt by updating the `archLabellerARM64` structure to drop `shouldLabelNodes()` since it returns true for all arches.
Previously, the `node-labeller` was disabled for ARM64 clusters due to incomplete support for labels like CPU features and models, which are supported on other architectures such as `amd64` and `s390x` - ref https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-88219.

For this PR, we’ve chosen to enable only machine-type labels for ARM64, as these are critical for virtual machine (VM) scheduling and represent the minimum functionality required from the `node-labeller`.

Note that machine-type labels were not required on arm64 clusters previously because VM scheduling on ARM64 did not depend on them. This changed after #13690 was merged, introducing functionality that relies on machine-type labels for proper VM scheduling.

Machine types are retrieved from the libvirt capabilities.xml, which is reliably available on ARM64 nodes. These values can be safely processed by the node-labeller without introducing risk or other issues.

Other labels supported by `node-labeller` on `amd64` and `s390x` (listed down) are intentionally ignored for ARM64 to minimize risk and focus on essential functionality. Support for additional labels may be added in future PRs.

Currently, the only supported label on ARM64 is:

- SupportedMachineTypeLabel

The following labels are not supported for ARM64 in this PR:
- CPUFeatureLabel
- CPUModelLabel
- CPUModelVendorLabel
- SupportedHostModelMigrationCPU
- CPUTimerLabel
- HypervLabel
- RealtimeLabel
- SEVLabel
- SEVESLabel
- HostModelCPULabel
- HostModelRequiredFeaturesLabel
- NodeHostModelIsObsoleteLabel

Fixes #

### Release note
```release-note
Enable node-labeller for ARM64 clusters, supporting machine-type labels.
```

body:
### 🛠️ Description of Changes

The overall objective of this PR is to provide better awareness of configuration changes introduced by the development team to the DevOps team. This will act as a heads-up that a config change may be needed in one or more of the environments that they manage. The changes are two-fold:
1. Added file patterns in the CODEOWNERS file covering changes to the `docs/config` folder and `docs/README.md` file, along with adding the `lantanagroup/devops` team so that they are included as reviewers to PRs in which matching files are changed. The DevOps team are not obligated to perform the review; they are added only so they get visibility of changes that may impact their work.
2. Add new `labeler` action with supporting config and workflow yaml files to automatically add a specific label to PRs with potential configuration changes. More information on the `labeler` action can be found [here](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/labeler).

The set of open PRs where there is a potential config change present can be seen in a dashboard view like [this](https://github.com/lantanagroup/link-cloud/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3Aconfig-change+is%3Aopen).

### 🧪 Testing Performed

1. Verified that members of the DevOps team are added to a PR as reviewer. The PR contained a documentation change (for test purposes only). See screenshot and actual PR here: https://github.com/lantanagroup/link-cloud/pull/793

author: shaunanoordin
body:
## PR Overview

Closes #7295

Staging branch URL: https://pr-7298.pfe-preview.zooniverse.org/lab/1982/workflows/editor/3711?env=staging

This PR updates the build process so that bundled image files are served from the `/lab` subpath, instead of the more sensible `/` root. Why change the path? Because we've configured the `www.zooniverse.org` domain to serve PFE code and FEM code on different paths, and the `/` root path is now the domain of FEM. Why the 'lab' subpath? Because in practice the only part of PFE that still uses bundled image files is the new Pages Editor.

- Changes are made to webpack.build.js (used for `www.zooniverse.org`) and webpack.dev.js (used on our local dev servers, i.e. on npm start)
- The changed subpath works properly on local, will work properly on the PFE staging link, but we won't know if the full production build will work properly until this PR is merged and deployed. ⚠️ 

### Testing

- Open the staging branch URL above ☝️ 
- On that Pages Editor page, you should see images (the Zooniverse word logo on the top right, and Task icons) served properly.
- You should not see broken images _anywhere_ on the Zooniverse.

author: stubbs41
body:
## Changes

This PR fixes the download scripts that were causing the Vercel build to take over 30 minutes. The issue was that the scripts were using an incorrect URL structure to download card data from the Pokemon TCG GitHub repository.

### Key Changes

1. **Fixed URL Structure**:
   - Updated the URL structure to use the correct path: `/cards/en/{setId}.json` instead of `/cards/{setId}/en.json`
   - This ensures that the scripts can successfully download card data

2. **Limited Download Size**:
   - Added a limit to download only the 20 most recent sets (instead of all 164 sets)
   - Limited the number of cards per set to 20 for image downloads
   - These limits keep the build time reasonable while still providing enough data for the application

3. **Improved Logging**:
   - Added more detailed logging to help diagnose issues
   - Added metadata about the limited download to help identify when new sets are available

4. **Vercel Configuration**:
   - Updated the Vercel configuration to better handle the build process

These changes should significantly reduce the build time while still providing enough data for the application to function properly.
